messages:
pagerduty-bot: Incident page triggered: elevated error rate on public inference API (5xx + 429s). Pager: oncall-sre. Severity: P1.
Sasha: seeing a sharp jump in 5xx and timeouts across gateway nodes starting ~3965432090. 5xxs are mostly 502/504 and a growing number of 429s. Top symptom: generation endpoints timing out at the gateway with long backend latency.
Cheng: logs show backend model pools returning 503s and redis KV latency spiking. snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T18:01:23Z INFO request_id=abc123 model=redwood-latest latency_ms=11234 status=502
2026-03-15T18:01:25Z WARN cache_hit=false redis_ms=1200
2026-03-15T18:01:27Z ERROR token-shedder drop=true reason=rate_quota_exceeded
```
Lina: can we confirm if a rate/quota config change rolled? I noticed a config push earlier to the rate-service at 17:55. @Alex did you touch global rates?
Alex: I deployed a small change to tighten per-tenant burst limits for the experimental throttling feature at 17:55 — intended to reduce noisy tenants. I didn't expect global pull-through to affect warm pools. Rolling it back now.
Sasha: rollback work in progress — thanks. In parallel, we need mitigations: 1) open emergency L7 rule to lift per-tenant burst caps for dedicated customers, 2) warm a subset of model pools and route high-SLA tenants there, 3) enable SLO protection to prioritize in-flight requests.
Mike: I'm on the pager and attaching: 1) increasing priority for top-5 tenants via routing whitelist, 2) toggling aggressive KV-caching for prefix hits, 3) temporary raise of gateway upstream timeout from 10s -> 25s to avoid cascaded 504s while pools stabilize. On it now.
Cheng: redis is taxed because of a bad cache eviction pattern from the new rate limiter. Current redis ops p90 = 1.3s. Scaling replicas now: `kubectl scale deployment/redis-cluster --replicas=6 -n infra` and rebalancer firing.
Lina: customer impact — monitoring shows three enterprise tenants (tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-c) have >30% failed requests and latency >8s; lower-tier tenants saw more 429s. No data leakage. I've messaged account teams to pre-emptively notify customers for tenant-a and tenant-b.
Sasha: note for handoff: primary mitigation sequence executed: rollback rate-config (Alex), scale redis (Cheng), increase gateway timeouts (Mike), enable SLO protection and routing whitelist (Mike/Sasha). Observed drop in 429s after rollback but backend 5xx still creeping.
Alex: rollback complete. rolling back config commit id `rfc-3172` and redeploying rate-service 17:58.
Cheng: redis scaled; rebalancer reports 6/6 ready. KV latency improved p90 -> 120ms. backend 503s reduced but some GPU pools still show queuing and OOM-like restarts on worker-12.
Mike: worker-12 is in a crashloop due to OOM on quantized kernel; draining it and moving traffic: `infractl pool drain worker-12 && infractl pool add-capacity pool-warm +2`. Doing canary traffic to warm pool.
Sasha: good. Also enabling model fallback policy to route to smaller quantized variant for non-realtime tiers: `policy.fallback:model=redwood-lite-v1` for non-SLA routes. This should reduce backend memory pressure.
Lina: Customer comms: tenant-a: degraded (retries recommended), tenant-b: partial outage, tenant-c: moderate errors. Sending consolidated update in 20m after second-wave checks.
Cheng: after drain, worker-12 restarted healthy. Error rate down 70% over the last 3 mins. 5xxs still ~2.5% on the busiest gateway, down from 12%. 429s mostly eliminated for whitelisted tenants.
Mike: putting a short-lived global circuit-breaker on public free-tier routing to shed load: `ratecfg set public.free burst=30 -> 5` and enable token-shedder aggressive=true. This protects SLO for paid customers.
Sasha: handoff to Mike for next 2 hours — concise summary: rollback rfc-3172, scaled redis, drained+replaced worker-12, increased upstream timeout, enabled fallback models, whitelist routing for top-5 tenants, temporary circuit-breaker on free-tier. Remaining work: postmortem, root cause (rate limiter eviction bug + tightened burst config), long-term fix (improve allocator, better canary for rate pushes), expanded warm pool for quantized models.
Mike: taking over. I'll monitor metrics for 60m and coordinate postmortem doc. tagging @cheshire-eng for allocator review.
Alex: follow-up — I'll author the postmortem section about the rate-config PR and add tests to simulate eviction spike.
Lina: escalation note: no new pages expected unless regressions; opening INC-2026-153 for tracking and customer comms. Adding links: dashboards: https://grafana/redwood/incident/3965432100, logs: https://logs/redwood/query?q=3965432100.
Sasha: thanks team. Quick check: any evidence of related region failover effects? Cheng?
Cheng: multi-region ingress behaved; we saw traffic shift from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 for ~30s before policies stabilized. No cross-region token leak.
Mike: I'll keep connection to oncall-sales for customer updates. handoff complete.
pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged handoff. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. If service degrades again, re-page oncall-sre.
